projects.title: TrussCraft
projects.subject: Physics · Statics
projects.tagline: Build a bridge. Run the load test. Watch the forces.
projects.description: A bridge-building game for teaching statics. Students lay roadway, timber, steel and cable across a gorge, then send a truck over while every member lights up blue in tension or red in compression. Each of the seven levels forbids the last level's answer, and every budget was set by searching for the cheapest bridge that actually survives.
features: Seven levels, from triangulation to cantilevers
Live Verlet physics with Euler buckling
Every failure explains which member gave way, and why
One offline HTML file: no install, no libraries
projects.caption: Live truss under a moving load. Blue is tension, red is compression. Drag a joint to load it yourself.
projects.alt: Animated truss bridge with a truck crossing it; members glow blue in tension and red in compression.

pricing.note: Free forever. No account, no ads, works offline.

projects.title: Like Terms Match
projects.subject: Maths · Algebra
projects.tagline: A neon match-three where only like terms combine.
projects.description: Swap tiles on a rotating 3D board to line up three or more like terms and simplify them. Coefficients don't matter, only the pronumeral and its power, which is the whole lesson. PEMDAS bombs clear rows and columns, divide-by-zero traps cost you shields, and the colour-coding fades away as students level up.
features: Scaffolding that fades as students improve
Arcade high-score table, initials and all
projects.caption: A real match-three engine finding swaps and simplifying. Move your pointer to tilt the board.
projects.alt: A tilted neon grid of algebraic terms; groups of three like terms light up and combine.

pricing.note: Free forever. Built to be played in class, on any device.

projects.title: Classroom Noise Monitor
projects.subject: Behaviour · Wellbeing
projects.tagline: A volume meter the whole class can see, so nobody has to shout.
projects.description: Turns any device's microphone into a friendly, real-time noise meter for the projector. A colour-changing creature, quiet challenges, attention signals and end-of-lesson reports let a class see how loud the room is and regulate itself. Audio is analysed on the device and never recorded, uploaded or stored.
features: Presets for library, group work, presentations and tests
Quiet challenges, achievements and session grades
Privacy first: audio never leaves the browser
projects.caption: A simulated classroom. Press “Use my mic” to drive it with your own room; the audio stays in this tab.
projects.alt: A circular volume gauge with a smiling creature in the middle that changes colour as the simulated room gets louder.

pricing.note: Free forever. Nothing to sign up for, and audio never leaves the room.

projects.title: Band 6
projects.subject: All HSC subjects
projects.tagline: An AI marker that grades like a senior HSC examiner, then shows you the next band.
projects.description: Students answer an HSC question and get it marked against the NESA band descriptors by a deliberately ruthless marker. A response that describes when the question says analyse is capped at Band 3, however long it is, and every mark comes with specific Band N+1 feedback. Teachers get a syllabus navigator, a question generator and an audit that fills gaps across a whole course.
features: Marks against NESA band descriptors and command verbs
Specific Band N+1 feedback on every response
Syllabus navigator down to individual dot points
Offline-first, with classes, quotas and a choice of AI providers
projects.caption: A “describe” answer to an “analyse” question: marked, capped, then rewritten a band higher.
projects.alt: A typed exam answer on lined paper being annotated in red pen, with a six-bar band meter rising from Band 3 to Band 5.

pricing.note: Priced for the HSC year: students pay while it matters, schools pay once for everyone.

projects.title: Maths Suite
projects.subject: Maths · Stage 4–5
projects.tagline: Differentiated maths worksheets from a seed, exported as vector PDF.
projects.description: Pick a stage, topics and NESA outcomes, and Maths Suite generates easy, medium and hard question sets with an answer key and optional worked solutions. Thirteen topics from integers to trigonometry, with geometry diagrams drawn on the fly. Every set comes from a seed, so the same seed always rebuilds the same worksheet.
features: 13 topics across Stage 4, Stage 5 and the 5.3 path
Filter questions by NESA outcome code
Seeded and reproducible, so a seed is a shareable worksheet
projects.caption: A seeded generator. The same seed always produces the same questions.
projects.alt: A maths worksheet whose seed number rolls over while fresh questions, including a right-angled triangle diagram, appear.

pricing.note: Free for a worksheet a week. Pro when it becomes part of your routine.

projects.title: Puzzle Suite
projects.subject: Literacy · Vocabulary
projects.tagline: Type in one word list, get a whole vocabulary pack.
projects.description: Type a list of words and clues and get a matching vocabulary sheet, word search, crossword, word scramble and answer keys, laid out and exported as a single vector PDF. Bulk export makes a unique set for every student, and AI can suggest a word list from a topic if you bring your own key.
features: Notes, word search, crossword, scramble and answer keys
Auto-placed crosswords that fit on one page
Bulk export of unique sets for a whole class
AI word lists with your own Gemini, Claude, OpenAI or Groq key
projects.caption: Words placed, then found. In the real app the generator runs in a Web Worker.
projects.alt: A word search grid being generated, with highlighter strokes finding each vocabulary word in turn.

pricing.note: The free tier is a complete tool. Pro is for teachers making packs every week.

projects.title: Software Engineering Notes
projects.subject: HSC Software Engineering · Y11–12
projects.tagline: Every dot point of the HSC Software Engineering course, written to be read.
projects.description: A free study guide for NSW HSC Software Engineering covering every Year 11 and Year 12 topic. It includes an SDLC guide with case studies from Spotify to the Boeing 737 MAX, and exam advice mapped to the NESA command verbs. The diagrams are written in Mermaid, so the flowcharts, class diagrams and state machines are all readable source.
features: SDLC guide with success and failure case studies
Mermaid flowcharts, DFDs, class and state diagrams
Glossary, dark mode and exam command verbs
projects.caption: Linear search, traced step by step through its flowchart and its NESA-style pseudocode.
projects.alt: A flowchart and pseudocode for linear search, with a marker stepping through each node while an array pointer moves along.

pricing.note: Free forever for every NSW student.
